items.name: Greater galangal
items.prabhava: The voice root — kulanjana is the traditional remedy for hoarseness, chewed by singers and orators; a fiercer, more aromatic cousin of ginger.
combinations: small piece chewed with honey for throat and voice
in kadha (decoction) for wet coughs
with black pepper for stubborn kapha
items.preparation: Dried rhizome in decoctions or a small fresh piece chewed slowly. Stronger and more resinous than ginger — dose in grams, not slices.

items.name: Indian sarsaparilla
items.prabhava: The sherbet root of the South — sariva cools blood and skin from within; classical raktashodhaka for pitta rashes, summer heat and burning urine.
combinations: nannari sherbet with lemon (the Madras summer drink)
with ushira and chandana in cooling infusions
milk decoction for pitta skin conditions
contraindications: very weak agni in decoction quantity
items.preparation: Fragrant root as cold infusion, syrup (sherbet) or milk decoction. The classical answer to summer pitta — skin, blood and urinary heat.

items.name: Vetiver root
items.prabhava: Ushira turns a pot of water into a summer medicine — the classical dahaprashamana root steeped in drinking water to quell burning, thirst and sweat-heat.
combinations: a knot of khus in the clay water pot (the classic)
in shadanga paniya (six-herb fever water)
khus sherbet with rock sugar
items.preparation: A small bundle of washed roots steeped in drinking water or matka; refreshed every day or two. Summer's most economical cooling therapy.

items.name: Sea buckthorn berry
items.prabhava: The Ladakhi high-altitude berry — Amchi (Tibetan) medicine's lung-and-blood tonic, intensely sour and oil-rich; a regional rasayana of the cold desert.
combinations: juice with honey (cuts the sharp sourness)
in herbal teas with rosehip
seed-oil taken separately for skin and mucosa
items.reviewNote: Primarily an Amchi/Sowa-Rigpa dravya, not classical Ayurveda; facets assigned by rasa-guna reasoning from the fresh berry.
items.preparation: Juice, syrup or dried-berry infusion; the pulp oil is used therapeutically. Sour and bracing — sweeten with honey and take in the cold months.

items.name: Amla murabba
items.prabhava: Rasayana in preserve form — sugar-curing softens amla's sharp sourness into a daily tonic the old texts' spirit approves for pitta and the modern palate accepts.
combinations: one piece each morning through winter (traditional course)
with warm milk after
silver-leafed festive versions
items.preparation: Whole amlas pricked, blanched and matured in sugar or honey syrup with saffron and cardamom. One fruit a morning; the syrup is not the medicine, the fruit is.

items.name: Haritaki murabba
items.prabhava: The king of medicines made gentle — sugar-cured haritaki keeps its anulomana (downward-guiding) grace while losing its rough dryness; classical texts prescribe haritaki with sweeteners by season.
combinations: one piece after the evening meal for gentle bowel regularity
with warm water in the morning
seasonal anupana tradition (jaggery in autumn, dry ginger in monsoon)
items.preparation: Young haritaki fruits softened and matured in sugar syrup. The murabba form suits delicate digestions that the raw churna would scrape.

items.name: Bael murabba
items.prabhava: Bilva's grahi (gut-binding) virtue in preserve form — the traditional keep-at-home remedy for chronic loose digestion and a gentle gut soother.
combinations: one piece with warm water for irritable digestion
before travel (traditional gut insurance)
with a pinch of dry ginger for cold-damp guts
items.preparation: Half-ripe bael pulp segments matured in sugar syrup. Classical bilva works best half-ripe — the murabba preserves it at exactly that stage.

items.name: Ginger murabba
items.prabhava: Vishvabheshaja sweetened — ginger's universal-medicine pungency wrapped in syrup; the winter preserve for weak appetite, cold coughs and travel nausea.
combinations: one piece before meals to rouse appetite
with warm water for morning sluggishness
traditional companion to winter breakfast
items.preparation: Tender ginger slices blanched and matured in sugar syrup with lemon. Deepana wrapped in sweet — the appetite of ginger without its raw burn.

items.name: Ash gourd murabba (petha)
items.prabhava: The classical medhya preserve — kushmanda candied is the traditional brain-and-nerve nourisher, the base of kushmanda rasayana for depleted minds and bodies.
combinations: a piece with warm milk (students' tradition)
kushmanda rasayana / avaleha in formal practice
kewra-scented Agra style
items.preparation: Ash gourd cubes limed, blanched and candied in syrup. Cooling, building, calming — morning food for the studious and the depleted, in ones and twos.

items.name: Green peas in pod (fresh sabzi)
combinations: cooked with ghee, cumin and hing (vata insurance)
whole-pod winter sabzi with ajwain
with paneer or potato in gravies
contraindications: vata excess / gas-prone (never without fat and spice)
items.preparation: Tender winter pods cooked whole or shelled, always with ghee, cumin and hing — legume astringency needs the classic vata counterweights.

items.name: Tender mustard pods
combinations: stir-fried with garlic and dried chili
mixed into saag
with makki roti in the sarson season
contraindications: thyroid caution with heavy brassica intake (folk-modern note)
items.preparation: Young seed pods of the mustard plant, stir-fried or folded into winter greens. Pungent-warming — kapha's winter friend, pitta's occasional visitor.

items.name: Indian gherkin (kundru-dondakaya kin)
combinations: stir-fried with mustard and curry leaves
in sambar-family stews
pickled young (regional)
items.preparation: Small spiny cucumbers of the gherkin type, cooked as everyday sabzi or added to stews. Light, watery, gently cooling — an easy vegetable for hot months.

items.name: Punjabi tinda (apple gourd)
combinations: simple jeera-tomato sabzi
stuffed tinda (Punjabi style)
in summer khichdi for the convalescent
contraindications: none significant — among the gentlest of gourds
items.preparation: Tender apple gourds peeled and cooked soft with cumin and mild spices. Summer sickroom-grade vegetable: watery, light and unconditionally easy on agni.

items.name: Wild brinjal (kantakari class)
items.prabhava: Kitchen relative of the dashamula pair (brihati-kantakari) — the bitter wild eggplants eaten as sabzi carry a whisper of their kapha-clearing, chest-opening medicine.
combinations: fried crisp with mustard oil and garlic (tribal/regional style)
in bitter-forward mixed sabzis
with rice and ghee to buffer the bitterness
items.preparation: Small bitter wild brinjals cooked thoroughly — never raw — usually fried or curried with assertive spicing. Eat as an occasional bitter tonic vegetable, not a staple.

items.name: Tender tamarind pod
combinations: pounded into chutney with green chili (Andhra chintakaya pachadi)
in tart spring dals
with jaggery to blunt the sourness
items.preparation: Immature green tamarind pods, fiercely sour, used pounded in chutneys and tart curries. Season-marker food of late winter; condiment quantities suit it best.

items.name: Fresh hyacinth beans (lilva)
combinations: star of undhiyu (the Gujarati winter pot)
with ajwain and garlic (traditional carminatives)
steamed with muthiya dumplings
items.preparation: Fresh winter beans shelled from papdi pods, cooked with the carminative spices Gujarat wisely never omits. A seasonal delicacy with a legume's flatulent streak.

items.name: Cashew apple
items.prabhava: The Konkan-Goa juice fruit — astringent-sweet false fruit of the cashew, pressed fresh or fermented; its tannic bite puckers before it pleases.
combinations: fresh-pressed juice with salt (Konkan style)
in regional curries (Goan style)
salt rubbed on slices to tame the tannins
items.preparation: Ripe cashew apples juiced or cooked; salting draws out the tannins. A coastal seasonal food — eaten in its brief hot-season window.

items.name: Sword bean
combinations: young pods sliced thin and curried with coconut
with garlic and ajwain (gas counterweights)
parboiled before final cooking (traditional detox step)
contraindications: mature beans undercooked (contain antinutrients — always boil well)
items.preparation: Only young tender pods, sliced and well cooked — mature sword beans need parboiling with the water discarded. A robust vegetable that demands thorough cooking.

items.name: Ash plantain
combinations: mild coconut-milk curry (Sri Lankan style)
steamed as bland diet for irritable guts
with cumin and turmeric, lightly tempered
items.preparation: Pale cooking plantain of the ash type, steamed or mildly curried. Gut-gentle and unassertive — a convalescent-friendly starch of the southern coasts.

items.name: Raw mango (sabzi/dal use)
items.prabhava: The classical unripe amra — intensely sour, appetite-rousing; cooked into dals and panna it becomes summer's tart shield, and in excess, pitta's provocation.
combinations: boiled into aam panna with roasted cumin (heat-stroke folk remedy)
in tart summer dals (mamidikaya pappu)
with jaggery — the traditional sour-sweet balance
contraindications: sore throat (classical caution on unripe mango excess)
items.preparation: Green mango cooked into dal, panna or sabzi — cooking with jaggery and cumin civilises the raw sourness. Classical texts warn against eating unripe mango raw in quantity.

items.name: Raw karonda (pickle berry)
combinations: stir-fried with green chili (karonda-mirch sabzi)
pickled (the classic use)
in tart chutneys with jaggery
items.preparation: Firm sour berries cooked as tart relish-sabzi or pickled. Classical karamarda is an appetiser-class sour — small amounts to wake agni, not bowlfuls.

items.name: Pink elephant yam
items.prabhava: Regional cousin of classical surana — the yam the texts single out for haemorrhoids (arsha); the pink strain shares suran's sharp, kapha-cutting nature.
combinations: boiled with tamarind or amchur (neutralises the itch-causing raphides)
mustard-oil fry with ajwain
in spiced winter curries
contraindications: skin itching if under-cooked or unsoured (calcium oxalate)
items.preparation: Always boiled with a souring agent before final cooking — tamarind tames the acrid raphides. A dense winter tuber for strong middays.

items.name: Ash gourd (juicing flesh)
items.prabhava: Kushmanda fresh-pressed — the modern morning juice with classical credentials: medhya (mind-nourishing), cooling to pitta, soothing to acid and heat.
combinations: fresh on an empty stomach (contemporary protocol)
a pinch of rock salt or pepper for cold constitutions
with mint in high summer
contraindications: cold, congested kapha constitutions (add pepper, or skip)
items.preparation: Mature ash gourd flesh juiced fresh, 100–150 ml on an empty stomach. Cooling and mildly agni-dampening — a summer-and-pitta therapy, not a winter habit.

items.name: Tender bamboo (fresh, unfermented)
combinations: boiled twice, water discarded (essential detox step)
curried with coconut (Karnataka kalale palya)
with sesame in tribal preparations
contraindications: raw or single-boiled shoots (cyanogenic — always double-boil)
items.preparation: Fresh monsoon shoots sliced and boiled in changes of water before currying — the bitterness and the toxins leave together. Distinct from the fermented sour shoot.

items.name: Water lily stem
items.prabhava: Pond-food of the classical texts — kumuda and utpala stalks are counted among the cooling, pitta-quelling foods of the water gardens.
combinations: in tangy fish-free curries (Bengal/Andhra pond-vegetable style)
with mustard paste (Bengali)
yogurt-based summer preparations
items.preparation: Peeled lily stalks cut and curried; mildly sweet, faintly mucilaginous, deeply cooling. A seasonal water-vegetable for hot climates and hot constitutions.
